detector.detectionDefinition: detected ⇔ source !== "none" ∧ ignoredNoise === false ∧ activeQuestion non-empty ∧ cleanedQuestion non-empty ∧ confidenceScore > DETECTION_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD (strict)

corpus.description: 120 labeled interviewer/candidate utterances covering direct questions, unpunctuated indirect questions, follow-ups, and four hard-negative classes (small talk, call admin, candidate statements, coding discussion). Includes tricky items: statements containing embedded question words (how/what/which/explain) and technical questions containing words the call-admin regex used to swallow (latency/network/connection/frozen).

heuristicChanges.change: isQuestion(): replaced unanchored substring matching over 20 question words with (a) '?' check, (b) start-word check against QUESTION_START_WORDS (wh-words, auxiliaries, interview imperatives such as tell/walk/design/give/write/continue), and (c) word-boundary matching for EMBEDDED_QUESTION_OPENERS.
heuristicChanges.rationale: Substring matching made statements containing 'how'/'which'/'when'/'explain' fire (e.g. 'My code creates a new array ... which causes re-renders', 'I explained how the cache invalidation worked') and made unpunctuated imperatives ('Walk me through ...', 'Design a ...', 'Continue from ...', 'Write a function ...') not fire.

heuristicChanges.change: ADMIN_NOISE_RE rewritten to match explicit call-management phrases only; bare device/network words (camera, mic, connection, network, latency, lag, frozen, ...) no longer suppress a whole utterance.
heuristicChanges.rationale: The old regex suppressed genuine technical questions such as 'How would you reduce tail latency in this service?' or 'How do you debug a frozen UI thread?'. Added explicit screen/audio/A-V phrases ('see my screen/cursor', 'share my screen', 'on mute', 'connection dropped', 'breaking up', 'link in the chat', 'ready to start').

heuristicChanges.change: Added SMALL_TALK_RE and wired it into build(): small talk is treated as noise (ignoredNoise=true) and receives the same -0.3 confidence penalty as admin noise.
heuristicChanges.rationale: Pleasantries phrased as questions ('how are you doing today?', "how's your day going?", 'how was your weekend?', 'how do you like the weather?') were confidently detected and would have triggered an answer. Requirement: never fire on small talk.

heuristicChanges.change: Added the evaluation harness: evaluateUtterance() calls the real detectActiveQuestion() live_interim path and applies the documented fire rule (source!=none ∧ !ignoredNoise ∧ non-empty activeQuestion/cleanedQuestion ∧ confidenceScore > 0.75); computeMetrics() builds utterance-level precision/recall.
heuristicChanges.rationale: G-016 had no labeled set and no metrics. 0.75 was chosen because the detector's own ladder puts statements at 0.70 and question-form utterances at 1.00.

knownLimitations: Measured at single-utterance level only. Multi-sentence merged STT snapshots are exercised by the existing detector tests but are not scored in this dataset.

The untouched check set contains one residual false positive: 'Is my audio coming through?' ('audio coming through' is not yet in ADMIN_NOISE_RE). It was deliberately left unfixed so the check set remains an honest post-freeze measurement; main-set thresholds are unaffected.

Heuristics are declarative regex/word-list rules, not a trained model. The rules were derived from the main set (and a later robustness pass informed by the holdout set); the untouched set is the closest thing to a blind measurement here.
The detector's confidence score is coarse (0.70 statement band vs 1.00 question band); the 0.75 threshold is a separating band, not a calibrated probability.
